A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sharp-Eyed Refinement and DeepLens research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original captioning and VideoQA evaluations, reconstruction experiments, attention visualizations, hardware measurements, and extensive appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional baseline scores and qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same OPT-125M specialist, frozen CLIP encoder, initial-caption MLP connector, and DeepLens refinement using initial captions and multi-layer visual features. Pseudo-caption generation, training objectives, and inference procedures remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate COCO, ShareGPT4V/DCI, GLaMM, and long-range VideoQA. The qualitative examples and deployment scenarios are retained; Jetson Nano evaluation already appears in v1 Appendix B.3.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Cambrian and ViPCap on COCO; its detailed-captioning comparison adds Cambrian and EyesWideShut while removing InstructBLIP. Table 3 replaces the detailed-captioning LLaVA comparator with Cambrian. SmolVLM joins the appendix visual-blindness comparison.

E3.justification: Matched appendix descriptions retain the dataset processing and sampling, metrics, training budgets, model configurations, and evaluation prompts. Additional comparator entries do not establish a revised evaluation protocol. Removing conflicting main-text dataset counts does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The visual-blindness case study adds SmolVLM and revises some displayed baseline captions, extending evidence about captioning errors (v1 Figure 13; v2 Figure 12). Connector, layer-selection, scaling, iterative-refinement, and pseudo-caption ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both specify 100 sampled images and 10 evaluation seeds for CLAIR and MLLM-as-judge, reporting means and standard deviations. New result rows follow this existing practice; no changed run count or statistical procedure is reported.

E6.justification: The specialist's principal scores remain unchanged, including SeR's 133.5 COCO CIDEr and 43.6 detailed-captioning CIDEr. New baseline results include Cambrian's 137.5 COCO CIDEr. Some qualitative baseline outputs change, and Table 2 loses LLaVA's previously reported detailed-captioning CLAIR 57.3±2.9 and GPT 3.00±0.10, leaving bare ± symbols.

T1.justification: Equation 1, the token-error set, the likelihood-margin argument, and the comparison with DPO are retained. There are no added or revised proofs, formal assumptions, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The central claims about lightweight captioning, visual grounding through DeepLens, and efficient refinement remain. v2 foregrounds long-range VideoQA in the abstract, but this contribution already appears in v1 Section 6 and Appendix A. The conclusion's 93% parameter and 97% inference-time reductions are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations involving diffuse attention and coarse visual features remain, alongside the same model-scaling interpretations and limitations concerning fluency, OCR, world knowledge, and evaluation metrics. Matching the appendices also establishes that the model-dependent interpretation of iterative refinement is retained.

D1.justification: v2 Figure 11 explicitly depicts positional embeddings, adding architectural documentation without establishing an implementation change. Section 5 drops the explicit promise to release pseudo-initial training captions. Conflicting main-text dataset counts are removed, while the appendix descriptions, hyperparameters, prompts, and code link remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to ViPCap, MoME, and VisionLLM v2 and removes two domain-adaptation/user-feedback references. It explicitly explains generalist versus specialist positioning. The visual-blindness related-work paragraph is relocated to Appendix B rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of Sections 1 and 3–6 are rewritten. Contributions are condensed, the setup subsection is reorganized, analyses receive explicit hypothesis/setup/result structure, and visual-blindness related work moves to a new appendix section. This is substantial editorial restructuring despite stable scientific content.

P2.justification: The training/inference diagram is redrawn and relocated, and the DeepLens architecture and connector variants are merged into v2 Figure 11. Qualitative displays, attention/reconstruction figures, captions, and highlighted notes are extensively reformatted. Evaluation prompts and pseudo-caption examples are separated across final appendix pages.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline comparisons and clearer organization and diagrams modestly improve comparative context and readability while preserving the substantive evidence. These gains are limited by new reporting defects: missing LLaVA judge scores in Table 2 and inconsistent Cambrian GPT scores between Tables 2 and 3 (3.03±0.09 versus 3.00±0.10). The revision improves presentation and context without resolving a major scientific deficiency.
